# CPU investigation — daemon PID 61945

Measure only. Deployed commit 8863651685; daemon started 2026-11-19 10:53:38 AEST. No code change, build/test, process kill, reload, daemon bounce or privilege escalation performed. Independent of PR #248.

## Findings

1. The recvfrom-heavy inference was incorrect: all 4296 recvfrom samples in the supplied 11:31:05 sample are two daemon-log threads parked in copy_timestamped -> BufReader<UnixStream>::read_until -> __recvfrom (2148 each). All 2140 plain read samples are the persistent pij-tmux-control reader parked on child stdout. These are sample occupancies, not syscall/request counts, and not inbound HTTP evidence.
2. The costly file path is UnisphereSessionStatus::status -> StatusService::status_incremental -> locate -> unisphere_core::prep::walk_prep_root -> Filesystem::list -> std::fs::read_dir -> opendir/open. Supplied sample: 1039/2148 samples on one blocking worker in status/locate, 993 in walker, including all 862 open samples. My second 5-second sample repeats it: 1218 samples status/locate, 1169 walker, 1020 open. Samples include IO waits and do not alone assign all CPU to that path.
3. One concrete bad status target is confirmed: pij-musical-hedgehog, live Copilot PID98769, session5256fe34-ff16-4676-b804-8fd87d75a87c, build ea5e9c49aa tree:4e6aee9ce4. Its canonical ~/.copilot/session-state/<session>/events.jsonl is absent. Metadata-only direct stats of all68 non-tombstoned Copilot rows found67 present,1 missing. One explicit diagnostic `pij-rs --json state pij-musical-hedgehog` took2.281s, reported liveness=active and sessionStatus.outcome=not-found / UNI-STATUS-TRANSCRIPT-NOT-FOUND. ps confirms the actual Copilot process began18Nov17:00:57, matching procStart20261118170057. This is a costly READ TARGET, not proof hedgehog is issuing the HTTP requests.
4. GET /v1/cards (or its implicit HEAD) is actively executing in both samples, including seat_cards -> seat_card -> active_holds -> EventBus/SqliteSpine::all_matching. Each request fans to every local untombstoned seat, reads status for every bound seat, and replays each seat's delivery-held/released/outcome history. Snapshot:127 non-tombstoned seats;42915 such delivery-history rows across120 seats per full cards request. This independently explains substantial SQL allocation/decoding work. The route is evidenced; its exact request rate and originating client are NOT currently measured.
5. Stale extension build does not by itself cause refusal: registration stores extension_build without comparing it. All parsed registration paths/counters remained unchanged across90.287s while CPU stayed high. The four named active Copilot reloads completed by11:32:09AEST, but CPU remained32.4–58.2% in the following minute. A missing transcript remains costly regardless of whether that seat reloads its extension.

## Live receipts

Times below are AEST unless marked UTC. Commands were run from /Users/jordanknight/pi-hacking/review-248-2bfd4dc.

Additional syscall-only process accounting, no launches in the sampled code: proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDLISTTHREADS=6 / PROC_PIDTHREADINFO=5) in libproc, from11:36:03.657 to11:36:20.517 (16.860s),70 common threads/no new threads. Summed actual user+system thread CPU=51.838% core. Three tokio workers account for8.887%,8.711%,8.648% core, mostly kernel time (each~1.32–1.36s system vs~0.13s user). Four sqlx-sqlite workers contribute~11.49% core total. The thread-list handles differ from sample's unique thread IDs; do not falsely map those handles to a named sample stack.

IMPORTANT: these are state-change/publication spine events, NOT exact POST /v1/activity request rates. Unchanged publications and refusals need not append an event. They are a lower-bound proxy only; the log and spine do not count GET /v1/cards at all. No request/sec claim is made for those uninstrumented routes.

### Extension builds and reload timing

Badger's measured rollout report: self reload11:19:45; asks to otter11:20:30, eagle/firefly by11:20:50; all four verified11:32:09 at build8863651685 tree:be14893ecf. Current SQLite rows agree for watchful-badger, steady-otter, sure-eagle, previous-firefly. Snapshot across all non-tombstoned rows: Copilot8 current build,60 older; Claude53; OMP5. Other cold/user seats were deliberately exempt, so the premise 'all seats current' has NOT been met fleet-wide. Old working rows include possible-porcupine and zoophagous-constrictor. Their presence does not imply retries; all registration deltas still0.

Earlier pre-rollout CPU receipt from this session11:16:59–11:17:19 (20.016s): CPUtime11:07.72->11:12.22,22.5% core; spawns781->781 and git placement28->28. This is not a controlled A/B because workloads and active seats changed. Reloads did not produce the hypothesized sustained drop in the observed later window.

### Routes and client attribution

- /usr/sbin/lsof -nP -iTCP:7461 -sTCP:ESTABLISHED identifies live Next server25506 and terminal-ws25518 as daemon clients alongside extension connections.
- /bin/ps and lsof cwd identify /Users/jordanknight/substrate/chainglass (Next cwd apps/web), not a guessed sibling checkout.
- Its rs-client.ts:186-191 issues GET /v1/cards. BUT start-pij-poller.ts:288-298 guards a process singleton and seeds once; RS mode disables legacy periodic loops. Only the seed calls cards in inspected source. Thus neither a fixed-cadence poller nor this particular client as the ongoing cards issuer is proven. Source/live-generation mismatch, other callers, and outstanding work remain alternatives.
- `~/.pij-rs/daemon.log` has no request access logs; last line observed01:12:23UTC is Telegram transport error, well before CPU window. Router has no general per-route/method/status/seat counters. Current extension clients do not log successful route calls.
- A read-only /usr/sbin/tcpdump lo0 probe failed immediately: /dev/bpf0 Permission denied, captured0bytes. No sudo/escalation attempted, no packets or credentials captured. Exact rates for cards and other read/refused routes cannot be recovered from current accessible telemetry. Lsof connections are not request counts.

## Source-backed mechanism and smallest fix shape

pij-unisphere src/lib.rs:177-180 sets transcript=None for every supported harness. Per-seat cursors are mutex-serialized. Success stores a located cursor; failures restore the previous cursor (214-228). The pinned unisphere commit0370cabbe4d9bcbb5b7bf6b0e13a490f0f4d0d59 SDK status.rs:793-820 probes canonical paths, but on a miss unconditionally calls discover(...,&Default::default()) at832-835. That is a cold recursive walk. TranscriptNotFound yields no negative cursor, so subsequent requests repeat it. Core walker has no directory-depth bound. Copilot's only accepted path is */events.jsonl and ID is the parent directory; no alternate walk can find the missing canonical session.

Preferred targeted fix: pass the explicit known Copilot transcript path in StatusTarget (SDK explicit path branch762-791 does one stat and returns NotFound), or fix upstream locate to stop after canonical Copilot miss. Preserve direct stat on every request so a newly created transcript becomes visible immediately; no arbitrary negative-cache freshness delay is needed for this layout. Do not paper over this by extending route timeouts, dropping the NotFound result, closing a real live seat, or merely reloading extensions.

For all harnesses, use one actual in-flight status operation per seat/target, not just a mutex queue of duplicate detached operations. Cards' four-slot semaphore bounds response waits only: at200ms the permit frees while work continues; later polls enqueue more cold misses. Existing positive cursors already avoid repeat successful discovery; adding another positive cache alone is not a fix. Missing noncanonical Claude/OMP/Codex sessions remain a broader locator/negative-cache tradeoff to investigate separately.

Separate server cost: active_holds replays42915 cumulative delivery rows per full cards request. Reuse an up-to-date bounded projection or ask only for live-held state rather than full histories on every read. Establish actual caller cadence before changing the client; current Chainglass source already seeds once and consumes events.

Needed measurement surface: bounded in-memory counts by HTTP matched route, method (HEAD separate), status class, and bounded known seat where available; plus status request/miss/discovery/in-flight counters keyed by seat/harness. Expose through health. No per-request spine/log write or subprocess. This lets the next measurement quote actual route/seat rates and distinguish raw arrivals from expensive work.

Proof ceiling: one verified missing Copilot target plus two matching discovery stacks and persistent >20% CPU support the targeted fix shape. They do not prove hedgehog accounts for all CPU or identify the actual cards request rate/caller. No destructive experiment or candidate deployment was authorized or performed.
